alcohol‐related disorders in middle age are associated with lower intelligence test scores in both young adulthood and in middle age, and with greater intellectual decline from young adulthood to middle age.

Individuals with alcohol‐ related disorders have a lower IQ both in young adulthood (baseline) and in late mid‐life, and these alcohol‐related disorders seem to be associated to a greater age‐related decline of IQ.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

individuals with alcohol‐ related disorders have a lower IQ in early adulthood and a larger age‐related decline, and these disorders are thus associated with a larger age‐dependent decline in intelligence test performance.

the lower intellectual ability observed in people with alcohol‐related problems is probably a result, not only of the disorders themselves, but also of the lower premorbid intellectual ability of those who later develop alcohol‐related problems.
